What was reviewed, and to what depth?

Not all 737 features received the same level of review. Here is what each status means:

  • Catalogue inclusion: The feature was listed in the original consumer genomics report and included in the audit.
  • Initial triage: The feature was assessed for scientific evidence, marker availability, and rule-development feasibility.
  • Abstract review: The abstract or summary of the source publication was consulted, but not the full text.
  • Full-text review: The full text of the source publication was reviewed for evidence extraction.
  • Evidence qualification: The feature had sufficient evidence quality and marker data for rule construction.
  • Technical audit: Allele contracts, build mapping, and strand orientation were verified.
  • Production-rule construction: A deterministic, executable rule JSON was produced and sealed.
  • Closed hold: The feature was scientifically relevant but could not be safely implemented due to unresolved metadata conflicts.

Interface coverage

This interface includes:

  • All 737 catalogue features with triage and status data
  • All 2,254 marker records with feature links
  • All 10 production rules with schema-aware display
  • All 5 closed holds with explanations
  • All 133 production regression and integration tests
  • 54 evidence records covering production-rule and closed-hold units
  • 387 provenance file records
  • 8 stage lineage records

Detailed evidence records shown here cover production-rule and closed-hold units; broader catalogue triage is represented in the Feature Catalogue.

Current result

  • 737 catalogue features catalogued and triaged
  • 10 production rules sealed (5 P25X1 + 3 P25AC + 2 P25AG1)
  • 5 closed holds (3 variant metadata conflicts + 2 multiallelic contract unresolved)
  • 133/133 production regression and integration tests passed
  • 0 active candidates remaining
  • No individual genotype interpretation
